first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.

actual_scope: Characteristic polynomial, over Q, of A_1 on the 84-dimensional X_3=+1 subspace of the trivial (+1,+1) joint space of the explicit c=3 pair.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for a formal caller or certificate binding. Open question 1 of PR #7020 asks for the characteristic polynomial of the 84-dimensional X_3=+1 subspace and names a basis of the joint equations as the first step. This package answers that polynomial. It does not add a Lean binding.
bottleneck_link: Scoped side result on the historical centre Gram. The selected conditional kappa remains 781451/250000000. The one-slot minimal polynomial remains degree 881 in research/exact-one-slot-gram/; this polynomial locates one invariant subspace inside that certificate and does not replace it.
stop_rule: Stop once one explicit 84-dimensional basis and the characteristic polynomial of A_1 on it are recomputed from the pinned query, with the matrix pinned and the factorisation checked. Do not rerun the degree-881 certificate or change the odd signs on the pair.
evidence: verify.py rebuilds the basis and the 84-by-84 integer matrix of B=4 A_1. Marker PASS_C3_X3_PLUS_CHARPOLY. chi_A SHA256 c4bcbd4e52f92d13f3ad451d92c9d22256e7725e4be24ee203bea1c96c129648. The degree-25 square-free product annihilates the matrix. Selected baseline returned PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY.

open_questions.question: What is the characteristic polynomial of the 132-dimensional X_3=-1 complement of this same trivial (+1,+1) joint space?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR #7020 splits the 216-space into dimensions 84 and 132. The polynomial computed here is only the eigenvalue-+1 half. The complement would meet the two published degree-88 sector polynomials.
open_questions.first_step: Impose X_3 eigenvalue -1 on the same joint equations for H, u and v, and repeat the signed orbit-sum matrix of B.
open_questions.blocked_by: The trace formula gives dimension 132 without listing a vector. This package stops at eigenvalue +1.

open_questions.question: What is the characteristic polynomial of one 66-dimensional intersection of that X_3=-1 complement with a single eigenvalue of Z_508?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 132-space is the sum of two 66-dimensional sector intersections. One 66-dimensional polynomial would sit inside a single degree-88 sector polynomial.
open_questions.first_step: Add the diagonal character Z_508 at one eigenvalue to the X_3=-1 equations and compute the 66-by-66 matrix of B.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not build the X_3=-1 basis, so it has no coordinates on which to impose Z_508.

overlap.limits: Closed PRs were searched through local READMEs, TASK metadata and the ledger. No code diffs or unpublished work. The phrase 84-dimensional matches PR #7020, which leaves this polynomial uncomputed, and does not match another open computation of it.
